title: Acts 9:32–43
context: Peter travels among the believers and comes to Lydda, where he heals Aeneas, bedridden for eight years, in the name of Jesus Christ, and the residents of Lydda and Sharon turn to the Lord. In nearby Joppa the disciple Tabitha, known for good works and charity, dies. The believers send for Peter, who prays and tells her to rise, and she comes back to life. Many in Joppa believe, and Peter stays there with Simon the tanner.

verses.text: As Peter went throughout all those parts, he came down also to the saints who lived at Lydda.
verses.arminianNotes: Peter travels among the saints and comes to Lydda. Arminian readers see apostolic care for scattered believers.
verses.reformedNotes: Reformed readers note that believers are called saints, set apart by God.

verses.text: There he found a certain man named Aeneas, who had been bedridden for eight years because he was paralyzed.
verses.arminianNotes: He finds Aeneas, paralyzed and bedridden for eight years. Arminian commentators see long suffering about to be relieved.
verses.reformedNotes: Reformed commentators see human helplessness awaiting God’s power.

verses.text: Peter said to him, “Aeneas, Jesus Christ heals you. Get up and make your bed!” Immediately he arose.
verses.arminianNotes: “Aeneas, Jesus Christ heals you.” He gets up immediately. Arminian readers see Peter pointing away from himself to Jesus.
verses.reformedNotes: Reformed readers see Christ himself as the one who heals.

verses.text: All who lived at Lydda and in Sharon saw him, and they turned to the Lord.
verses.arminianNotes: All in Lydda and Sharon see him and turn to the Lord. Arminian expositors see a sign prompting many to respond.
verses.reformedNotes: Reformed expositors see God using the miracle to bring people to himself.

verses.text: Now there was at Joppa a certain disciple named Tabitha, which when translated means Dorcas. This woman was full of good works and acts of mercy which she did.
verses.arminianNotes: Tabitha, or Dorcas, is full of good works and acts of charity. Arminian readers see faith expressed in practical love.
verses.reformedNotes: Reformed readers see good works as the fruit of grace in a disciple.

verses.text: In those days, she became sick and died. When they had washed her, they laid her in an upper room.
verses.arminianNotes: She becomes sick and dies, and they lay her in an upper room. Arminian commentators note the community’s grief.
verses.reformedNotes: Reformed commentators see death touching even the most faithful.

verses.text: As Lydda was near Joppa, the disciples, hearing that Peter was there, sent two men to him, imploring him not to delay in coming to them.
verses.arminianNotes: The disciples send for Peter. Arminian readers see faith that hopes for more than comfort.
verses.reformedNotes: Reformed readers see believers turning to God through his appointed servant.

verses.text: Peter got up and went with them. When he had come, they brought him into the upper room. All the widows stood by him weeping, and showing the tunics and other garments which Dorcas had made while she was with them.
verses.arminianNotes: Widows show Peter the garments Dorcas made. Arminian expositors see a life remembered by the people it served.
verses.reformedNotes: Reformed expositors see the visible fruit of a hidden faith.

verses.text: Peter sent them all out, and knelt down and prayed. Turning to the body, he said, “Tabitha, get up!” She opened her eyes, and when she saw Peter, she sat up.
verses.arminianNotes: Peter sends them out, prays, and says, “Tabitha, get up!” and she opens her eyes. Arminian readers note the echo of Jesus raising Jairus’s daughter.
verses.reformedNotes: Reformed readers see that Peter prays first, recognizing the power belongs to God.

verses.text: He gave her his hand and raised her up. Calling the saints and widows, he presented her alive.
verses.arminianNotes: He helps her up and presents her alive to the saints and widows. Arminian commentators see joy restored to the community.
verses.reformedNotes: Reformed commentators see a foretaste of the resurrection.

verses.text: This became known throughout all Joppa, and many believed in the Lord.
verses.arminianNotes: This becomes known throughout Joppa, and many believe. Arminian readers see the sign leading people to faith.
verses.reformedNotes: Reformed readers see God gathering his people through his works and word.

verses.text: He stayed many days in Joppa with a tanner named Simon.
verses.arminianNotes: Peter stays many days with Simon the tanner. Arminian expositors note that tanners were considered unclean, a hint of barriers about to fall.
verses.reformedNotes: Reformed expositors see God positioning Peter for the vision of chapter 10.
